AttachmentTrack.description:
An attachment's parameters.

A `path` attaches a new file to the output (using the `attachment_*` fields
as its name, description, and MIME type). Without a `path` the entry only
participates in copy selection; mkvmerge cannot rename or re-describe an
attachment that is copied from a source file.

copy.description: Whether to copy this attachment. Defaults to `true`.

path.description: A file to attach to the output.

copy.description: Whether to copy this track. Defaults to `true`.

max_memory.description: The maximum amount of RAM (in megabytes) allowed across all workers

threshold.description: Percent of speed increase required to add an additional worker

bitrate_sigma_threshold.description:
Standard Deviation distance from average scene bitrate to be considered
an excessively large scene

BorderHandling.description: Method for handling image borders during sampling.

Chapters.description:
Chapter handling.

`None` means "copy the source's chapters" (the default). When present,
`copy` controls whether source chapters are kept, and `language`/`charset`
override where mkvmerge would otherwise guess.

charset.description: Character set used to decode simple chapter files.

copy.description: Whether to copy chapters from the source. Defaults to `true`.

language.description: ISO 639-2 language code written for every chapter entry.

ChromaSampling.description:
Chroma subsampling that a native FFMS2 input can be converted to.

[`ChromaSubsampling`] carries no serde derives, so this is a local mirror,
as with [`ColorRange`] and [`PixelFormat`].

[`ColorRange`]: crate::core::input::color_range::ColorRange
[`PixelFormat`]: crate::core::input::pixel_format::PixelFormat

ConcatMethod.description:
The concatenation method and its output settings.

Each variant carries that muxer's track, chapter, and metadata settings, so
the settings live on the method itself rather than in separate properties
that could disagree with it.

oneOf.description: MKVToolNix mkvmerge, with its track/chapter/metadata settings.
FFmpeg, with its track/metadata settings and audio/subtitle filters.

FfmpegAttachmentTrack.description:
An attachment's parameters.

A `path` attaches a new file to the output (using the `attachment_*` fields
as its name, description, and MIME type) via FFmpeg's `-attach`. Without a
`path` the entry only participates in copy selection; FFmpeg cannot rename
or re-describe an attachment copied from a source file.

attachment_description.description:
The attachment's description. FFmpeg attachments have no dedicated
description element, so this is written as `comment` metadata.

attachment_mime_type.description: The attachment's MIME type (`mimetype`). Required when `path` is set.

attachment_name.description: The attachment's file name in the output (`filename`).

copy.description: Whether to copy this attachment. Defaults to `true`.

path.description: A file to attach to the output.

FfmpegConfig.description:
FFmpeg output settings for the Scene Concatenator.

Setting `ffmpeg: {}` in the configuration adds the original input (and any
extra inputs) to the output; leaving it unset keeps the video-only
concatenation.

chapters.description: Chapter handling. `None` copies the source's chapters.

extra_inputs.description: Additional files muxed alongside the encoded scenes.

tracks.description:
Per-stream overrides for the main input. `None` copies all audio and
subtitle streams.

FfmpegExtraInput.description: An additional source file muxed into the output.

tracks.description:
Per-stream overrides for this file. `None` copies all its audio and
subtitle streams.

FfmpegTrack.description: A track type and its FFmpeg options.

oneOf.description:
An attachment (FFmpeg's `t` stream type, mirrored from mkvmerge's
`AttachmentTrack`).

FfmpegTrackOptions.description: A single output stream's FFmpeg options.

codec.description:
Output codec for this stream (`-c:a:N` and friends). `copy` keeps the
source codec.

copy.description: Whether to copy this track. Defaults to `true`.

filter.description:
Filtergraph applied to this stream (`-filter:a:N` / `-filter:s:N`).

Rejected for video tracks. Requires a non-`copy` codec, because a
filtered stream has to be re-encoded.

parameters.description:
Extra FFmpeg arguments, appended verbatim. Each key must start with
`-` and must not override Condor's own arguments.

Ffms2Filter.description:
Filters available to natively-decoded (non-VapourSynth) FFMS2 inputs.

FFMS2 can only convert the frames when it decodes with
`Ffms2Decoder::set_output_format` to a target pixel format and resolution.

oneOf.description:
Sets the output resolution, bit depth and chroma subsampling.

Any field left `None` keeps the decoded value.

8/10/12-bit are supported across YUV420/422/444 and monochrome. A
request with no suitable output format is an error rather than a
silent substitution.

cache_path.description:
Where to read or write the `.ffindex` cache, defaulting to
`{source}.ffindex` next to the source file.

index.description:
The video track to decode, as seen by FFMS2. `None` selects the
first video track.

filters.description:
Conversion applied to the decoded frames.

Native FFMS2 cannot run arbitrary filters; this is the full set of
modifications it supports.
Filters chained onto the source node, in order.
Filters chained onto the script's output node, in order.

stream_concurrently.description:
Whether several encoders may pull frames from this script at once.

Streaming frames concurrently bounds memory, because only a fixed
window of frames is kept resident. Setting this to `false` decodes a
whole scene ahead of its encoders instead, trading memory for decode
speed, and is worth trying if the script's source plugin decodes
slowly under concurrent access.

Metadata.description:
Global metadata written to the output.

`None` on [`super::mkvmerge::MkvmergeConfig::metadata`] means "copy the
source's global tags" (the default). When present, `copy` controls whether
the source's own global tags are kept, and `title`/`tags` describe the
output's tags.

copy.description: Whether to copy global tags from the source. Defaults to `true`.

MkvmergeConfig.description: `mkvmerge` output settings for the Scene Concatenator.

chapters.description: Chapter handling. `None` copies the source's chapters.

extra_inputs.description: Additional files merged alongside the encoded scenes.

metadata.description: Global metadata/tags. `None` copies the source's global tags.

tracks.description: Per-track overrides for the main input. `None` copies all tracks.

MkvmergeExtraInput.description: An additional source file merged into the output.

chapters.description: Chapter handling for this file. `None` copies its chapters.

metadata.description: Metadata handling for this file. `None` copies its global tags.

tracks.description: Per-track overrides for this file. `None` copies all its tracks.

VapourSynthFilter.description:
The [`Degrain`](VapourSynthFilter::Degrain) variant is a composite filter
that intentionally carries many configuration fields, so the enum is larger
than the other variants.

oneOf.description:
MVUtensils Degrain - motion-compensated temporal denoising workflow.
This is a composite filter that internally chains Super -> AnalyseMany
-> (optional Recalculate) -> Degrain.

ZooMVTools Degrain - motion-compensated temporal denoising workflow.
This is a composite filter that internally chains ZMVSuper -> two
Analyse calls (isb=0 forward, isb=1 backward) -> (optional
Recalculate on both) -> Degrain1 (implemented as Degrain).

FGS (Film Grain Synthesis) - applies photon-noise film grain using
dav1d's grain engine. Builds a [`PhotonNoise`] from the supplied
parameters and delegates to the `com.vs.fgs` plugin's `FGS` function.

chroma_iso.description: Optional ISO strength for chroma grain (defaults to luma `iso`).

dynamic_seed.description:
When `true`, randomizes the grain seed per frame for dynamic
variation.

iso.description: Required ISO strength for the luma grain.

aspect_ratio.description:

`display_dimensions` and `aspect_ratio_factor`.

copy.description: Whether to copy this track. Defaults to `true`.
